title: CBC Theatre 10:30
paragraphs: A CBC radio-drama anthology represented here by a small collection of standalone plays. Because surviving catalog information is uneven, this description avoids assigning unsupported dates or a single recurring premise.

CBC dramatic anthology preserved in thirteen frozen recordings. Chronology is disputed: the preservation catalog treats the collection as 1961-era and one file is dated 1961-08-28, while other references place Theatre 10:30 in 1968-71.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: CBC Theatre 10:30 chronology-disputed run (1961 to 1971) on [[org|org.vp.4ad028d3bc03e0f3|CBC Radio]].
Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Anthony Lee Flanders (writer), Alan King (writer), and Betty Lambert (writer).

The stories often return to Canadian radio drama, classic literary adaptation, horror and supernatural fiction, science fiction and speculative fiction, wilderness and isolation, and psychological horror and obsession.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes CBC dramatic anthology tradition, Theatre 10:30 chronology dispute, Mid-century radio adaptation of classic horror and speculative literature, and Klondike gold-rush historical setting.

CBC dramatic anthology preserved in thirteen frozen recordings. Chronology is disputed: the preservation catalog treats the collection as 1961-era and one file is dated 1961-08-28, while other references place Theatre 10:30 in 1968-71.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: CBC Theatre 10:30 chronology-disputed run (1961 to 1971) on CBC Radio.

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Anthony Lee Flanders (writer), Alan King (writer), and Betty Lambert (writer).

The stories often return to Canadian radio drama, classic literary adaptation, horror and supernatural fiction, science fiction and speculative fiction, wilderness and isolation, and psychological horror and obsession.
